# Bullets from the players ship should always fall on the beat

## Problem statement

Player auto-fire currently uses per-weapon cooldowns started at collection time (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `Player.tryFire`), so shots drift relative to any musical pulse and different active weapons fire out of phase. Make every player shot land on a shared musical grid: player fire is globally quantised to an **80 BPM** beat, and every weapon's fire rate is an exact subdivision of that beat. The values are configurable rather than hard-coded.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the ship's shots to feel rhythmically locked to a consistent 80 BPM pulse, so the auto-fire has a musical cadence even with no background music.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a single, pure beat-clock module and a catalogue-wide invariant so any current or future weapon (e.g. the planned 20 BPM quarter-time large/explosive bullet) can be added without accidentally firing off the beat.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my ship's bullets to leave on the beat, so the auto-fire feels deliberate and rhythmic rather than mechanically drifting.
- As a **player**, I want every weapon I collect to keep firing in time with the same beat, so switching weapons never makes the rhythm stumble.
- As a **developer**, I want a weapon's fire rate to be expressed as a subdivision of the beat and validated by a test, so I cannot add an off-grid weapon by mistake.
- As a **developer**, I want the BPM and per-weapon subdivisions to be configurable, so the feel can be tuned (and tested) without editing hard-coded literals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.
- [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.
- [ ] **AC4 — All values configurable.** BPM, the per-weapon subdivisions/fire rates, and the quantisation behaviour are configurable through the project's existing config plumbing (`src/core/rules.ts` and/or `src/core/config.ts`/`constants.ts`; persisted where the existing pattern persists), with sane defaults — no scattered hard-coded beat/rate literals. Tests assert a config override changes the firing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the beat module (period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override), the catalogue invariant (AC3), and `Player.tryFire`/auto-fire emitting only on grid ticks with multiple active weapons phase-locked. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) assert real bullet spawns land on grid ticks across multiple frames and are framerate-independent. All tests serve a distinct behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries — in particular GDD §2.3/§4.4 (the "Cannon fires every ~400 ms" wording and the weapon fire-rate description) and any beat/config tuning docs.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). No external art/audio assets.
- **Silent timing grid only:** per producer, the beat is an internal scheduling contract — **no audible metronome and no background music** (GDD §7.3/§8 keep music out of MVP scope). No beat audio/visual indicator is in scope.
- **Player bullets only:** enemy fire timing is unchanged (the item is titled "from the players ship").
- **Scope:** applies to all scenes that auto-fire the player (PlayScene via `CombatScene`, and the gym scenes reusing `Player`), through one shared beat module — not per-scene duplicates.
- **Beat anchor:** the beat clock is anchored at scene/player start and advances with game time (pauses with the game if paused).
- **No behaviour change beyond timing:** weapon patterns, bullet visuals, lifetimes, cumulative+timed semantics and Reset behaviour are unchanged; only fire timing changes.

## Existing state

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` defines `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` with hard-coded `fireRateMs` (cannon 400, spread 600, dual 500, rapid 125) and `bulletLifetime` values; heading/pattern math is pure.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` holds per-weapon cooldowns in `_weaponCooldowns` and `tryFire(dt)` re-arms a fired weapon's cooldown to its own `fireRateMs` (independent timers, phase set by collection time). Cumulative + timed semantics (`equipWeapon`, `resetWeapon`, `tickWeaponTimers`) are implemented and tested.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`_autoFire`) and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` (`_autoFire`) call `player.tryFire(dt)` each frame and spawn bullets via `createBulletsFromHeading`/`angleToVelocity`.
- **No beat/BPM/clock infrastructure exists anywhere in `src/`**; there is no music system (GDD §7.3 out-of-MVP).
- Config precedent: `src/core/rules.ts` (localStorage-persisted `GameRules`, e.g. power-up spawn interval) and `src/core/config.ts`/`configTypes.ts` (CSV-backed ship config). `src/core/constants.ts` holds `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` etc.
- Related completed work: AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR (weapon catalogue + auto-fire), AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR (`tryFire` extraction), AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6 (cumulative/timed weapons), AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0 (bullet lifetimes).

## Desired change

1. Add a pure **beat module** (`src/utils/beat.ts`): BPM → beat period, beat anchor, and quantisation helpers (`nextSubdivisionTick`, `shotTimeFor`, `isOnGrid`). Configurable BPM (default 80).
2. Re-express each `WeaponDefinition` fire rate as a **beat subdivision** (cannon 2/beat, spread 1/beat, dual 1/beat, rapid 6/beat) derived from the beat period; add the catalogue-wide on-grid invariant test.
3. Replace per-weapon free-running cooldowns in `Player.tryFire` with **phase-locked scheduling**: a weapon's next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time (anchored at the shared beat origin), so every shot lands on a grid tick and active weapons stay in phase. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design).
4. Wire the shared beat clock into `CombatScene._autoFire` and `GymWeapons._autoFire` (and any other `Player.tryFire` callers) so the scene supplies/uses the same clock.
5. Make BPM and the per-weapon subdivisions **configurable** through the existing config plumbing with defaults, rather than literals.
6. Update unit + scene-harness tests (existing `weapons.test.ts`, `Player.test.ts`, `GymWeapons.test.ts`, `CombatScene` tests) and documentation (GDD §2.3/§4.4, README).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock + quantisation helpers.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates re-expressed as beat subdivisions; catalogue-wide on-grid invariant.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire`/cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — `_autoFire` drives the shared beat clock.
- `src/core/rules.ts` / `src/core/config.ts` (and/or `src/core/constants.ts`) — configurable BPM + per-weapon subdivisions with defaults.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts`, **NEW** `src/utils/beat.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — coverage for quantisation, invariant and scene emission.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3/§4.4; `README.md` — document the beat-aligned fire model.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Gameplay-feel change:** current rates (cannon 400 → 375 ms; spread 600 → 750 ms; dual 500 → 750 ms; rapid 125 unchanged) slightly change DPS/cadence, and collection now delays the first shot to the next grid tick. Assumption: acceptable and intended ("must always fall on the beat").
- **Definition of "the beat" without music:** resolved by the producer — silent internal grid; no audible/visual reference. The beat is only observable through bullet cadence and tests.
- **Config surface choice:** the producer requires configurability, but the exact home (localStorage rules vs CSV ship config vs constants) is a planning decision; the ACs require at least one tested override path.
- **Phase-locking and multiple weapons:** cumulative weapons with different subdivisions must share the anchor; an implementation that keeps independent cooldowns will drift — the AC2 test guards this.
- **Frame quantisation edge cases:** shots must be attributed to the correct grid tick under variable `dt` (including large deltas), and remain framerate-independent — explicit boundary tests required.
- **Scope-creep risk:** audible beat/music, enemy fire quantisation, and beat-synced visuals are out of scope; record as linked work items rather than folding in.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (completed) — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene": origin of `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, the fire-rate constants and `Player` auto-fire this item re-times.
- **AH-0MUD9R3070063DDR** (completed) — "Extract auto-fire with onWeaponFired hook": the `tryFire` auto-fire architecture being changed.
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** (completed) — "Make weapons both cumalative and time out": cumulative per-weapon timers/cooldowns.
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** (completed) — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen": per-weapon bullet lifetimes adjacent to the fire-rate config.
- **AH-0MTGS8TWU006WTFX** (completed) — "Wire shoot audio into GymWeapons._autoFire()": fire cues whose cadence follows the fire rate.
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed) — "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD": the audio-scope boundary (no music).
- **GDD (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — §2.3 auto-fire (~400 ms wording), §4.4 weapon fire rates/lifetimes, §7.3 audio (music out of scope), §8 future scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Beat semantics — (a) per-weapon beat-subdivision intervals with independent cooldowns, or (b) a single 80 BPM clock with every shot snapped to the next grid tick?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(b) global beat quantisation**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What is the beat reference — (a) silent internal grid only, (b) audible metronome, or (c) visual beat indicator?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **(a) silent internal grid only** (no music; consistent with GDD §7.3). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Per-weapon subdivisions and the catalogue-wide invariant?" — Answer (producer, interactive): **as recommended** — cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat), spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat), rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat); invariant `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` enforced for the whole catalogue. Source: interactive reply.
- Producer note (interactive, given alongside the answers to Q1–Q3): **all values must be configurable** (BPM, per-weapon subdivisions, quantisation behaviour). Source: interactive reply.

> Prior answers changed: none — all answers above are the final accepted versions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** – Bullets should have a distance and should wrap around the screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77** – GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev) (in-progress)
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, beat (+30 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, always, based, beat, bullet (+29 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, always, assert, based, belongs (+28 more)

## Plan (plan_complete)

stage `intake_complete`:

**Phase 1 — Foundation**
- Implement pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock module (AH-0MUGPSOVM006Z1OJ)

**Phase 2 — Grid + invariant**
- Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant (AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG)
- Make BPM and per-weapon subdivisions configurable via existing config plumbing (AH-0MUGY84L1004H2UP)

**Phase 3 — Emission + wiring**
- Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling (AH-0MUGQCMNA0061J4A)
- Wire the shared beat clock into CombatScene and GymWeapons auto-fire (AH-0MUGY7ZUO008QSUX)

**Phase 4 — Verification + handoff**
- Scene-level tests: verify real bullet spawns land on grid ticks (AH-0MUGY89LE006WVDQ)

**Dependency edges:** T2→T1, T3→T1, T4→T3, T5→{T1,T2}, T6→T4,
T7→{T2,T3,T4,T5}, T8→{T6,T7}.

# Intake Brief: Divers should not return (AH-0MUAYB957002EMYV)

## Headline

While a Diver is away from the formation on its dive attack, the whole enemy cluster must hold its current position (freeze its drift) and resume only once every Diver has rejoined; the Diver still returns, but to its slot in the *current* formation and never to the stale dive-start point.

## Problem statement

Divers dive out of formation toward the player, pause, then glide back to a formation that has kept drifting in the meantime. This reads as the Diver "chasing" a moving cluster and makes the return feel disconnected from the attack. The cluster should instead stop moving while a Diver is away, so the attack reads as: the formation holds, the Diver dives, pauses and rejoins the same (stationary) formation, and only then does the cluster continue on its way.

## Users

- **Player:** Reads the dive attack as deliberate — the formation hesitates, the Diver commits, and the Diver visibly re-forms with its group rather than chasing it.
- **Developer:** Gets a small, explicit "hold the formation" seam shared by the gym base scene and `PlayScene`, with deterministic tests.

Example user stories:

- *As a player, when a Diver dives at me the rest of its cluster stays put until the Diver has rejoined, so I can read where the formation is and plan my movement.*
- *As a developer, I want a single optional entity seam that tells a formation scene "hold the cluster this frame", so the gym and the shipped game cannot diverge.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — The formation holds while a Diver is away.** While any Diver is in a non-`FORMATION` state (`DIVING`, `PAUSING` or `RETURNING`), the formation base does not advance: `GymFormationScene.tick()` leaves `formationBaseX` unchanged (and does not fire the wrap/respawn), and `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` leaves `driftX`/`driftDir` unchanged. *Verification:* deterministic tests in `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` assert the base/drift is unchanged after ticks with a Diver in each non-formation state, and unchanged while a second Diver is still holding; a destroyed Diver (`alive === false`) in a non-`FORMATION` state must NOT hold the formation, so the gate must consider only living entities and a mid-dive kill cannot freeze the cluster forever.
2. **AC2 — The formation resumes once every Diver has rejoined.** As soon as no Diver is detached (all in `FORMATION`), the formation resumes moving from the frozen position with no jump/snap. *Verification:* a two-diver test asserts the formation stays frozen while one is away and continues from exactly the held `formationBaseX`/`driftX` once both are back.
3. **AC3 — Divers return to their slot in the current formation.** `Diver._handleReturn()` continues to glide onto the slot evaluated live from the formation base (`baseX + col * spacingX`, `baseY + row * spacingY`) and never to a stale dive-start coordinate; a returning Diver never relocates the cluster to meet it. *Verification:* a unit test asserts the return target re-evaluates the supplied base each frame; the existing smooth-return / no-jump tests (`AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD`, `AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB`) stay green.
4. **AC4 — Dive/return geometry and existing behaviour preserved.** The diagonal bezier dive toward the snapshotted player position, the 500 ms pause, the ~3 s hold, spread-shot firing, dive/pause/return rotation, audio and explosion behaviour are all unchanged, and non-Diver entities (Scout/Tank/Phaser/Swarm/Asteroid/Boss) behave exactly as before. *Verification:* the existing `Diver.test.ts` suites pass unmodified, and a scene test confirms a formation with no Diver still drifts.
5. **AC5 — Tests, docs and full suite.** New deterministic tests cover the hold seam and freeze/resume in both scenes; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and GDD §4.1 E2); the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Shared seam, both scenes.** Add an optional entity method (working name `requiresFormationHold?(): boolean`) to `FormationSceneEntity` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`) **and** to the shared `EnemyEntity` seam in `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` (alongside `DestructionAudioSeam`), so `PlayScene` can query it on the union type. Non-Diver entities omit it; call sites use optional chaining.
- **Two drift implementations must both be gated.** `GymFormationScene.tick()` (`formationBaseX`, rightward drift + wrap) and `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` (`driftX`/`driftDir`, ping-pong drift) are independent and must each consult the seam.
- **Keep the diagonal dive (Q3-A).** Do not change the dive shape, and do not fold in the open docs item `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` (GDD calls the dive vertical while the code is diagonal) — that stays a separate item.
- **No new audio/VFX and no timing/config-default changes.** Use the existing `DIVER_*` constants.
- **Freeze scope.** The hold applies for the entire detached window (`DIVING`, `PAUSING`, `RETURNING`); the formation must not wrap/respawn during a hold.
- **Out of scope:** closing formation gaps / restructuring the cluster's internal layout (`Q2-C`) and preventing wrap-only relocation (`Q2-D`) were not selected.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` runs a four-state machine (`FORMATION → DIVING → PAUSING → RETURNING → FORMATION`). The dive is a diagonal quadratic bezier from the formation slot to the player position snapshotted at dive start (`AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX`); the pause is 500 ms (`AH-0MU0EIDQQ003S1JT`); `_handleReturn()` glides from the dive target onto the slot evaluated each frame from the live `baseX`/`baseY` (`AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB`), so it already rejoins the drifting cluster without a snap.
- The formation base is advanced unconditionally: `GymFormationScene.tick()` does `formationBaseX += config.driftSpeed * dt` then wraps when it exceeds `GAME_WIDTH + 60`; `PlayScene._moveEnemies()` advances `driftX` with a `driftDir` ping-pong bounded by `FORMATION_DRIFT_RANGE`. Neither consults entity state.
- There is no seam today by which an entity can ask its scene to hold the formation.
- Open `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` records that GDD §4.1 still describes a vertical/x-locked dive while the implementation is diagonal (pre-existing, not caused by this item).

## Desired change

1. Give the `Diver` a way to report that it is detached from the formation (working name `requiresFormationHold()` returning `this._state !== DiverState.FORMATION`), published through the shared entity seam so both scenes can query it.
2. Gate the drift advance (and, in the gym scene, the wrap/respawn) on **no** entity requiring a hold. While held, the base stays fixed; every entity's `applyFormationPosition` still runs each frame with the unchanged base so the Diver can rejoin precisely.
3. Resume normal drift automatically on the first frame after the last detached Diver re-enters `FORMATION`.
4. **Hold only on living entities.** The two scene gates must ignore destroyed Divers: a Diver killed mid-`DIVING`/`PAUSING`/`RETURNING` must stop holding immediately so a dead Diver can never freeze the cluster. Implement the seam as `this.alive && this._state !== DiverState.FORMATION` (or filter `entity.alive` at both call sites) and cover it with a test.

Implementation order (test-first): (1) add the failing tests — the seam unit test in `Diver.test.ts` and the freeze/resume scene tests (single diver, two divers, destroyed diver, and no-Diver-still-drifts); (2) add the optional seam to `Diver` and to both entity interfaces (`FormationSceneEntity`, `EnemyEntity`); (3) gate the two drift sites; (4) run the full suite and update the docs (AC5).

No change is required to the Diver's return target logic — with the cluster frozen, the "current" slot is stationary, so the Diver lands exactly where it left.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — implement the `requiresFormationHold()` seam (true for `DIVING`/`PAUSING`/`RETURNING`); class JSDoc note on the hold behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — add the optional seam to `FormationSceneEntity`; gate the `formationBaseX` advance + respawn in `tick()` on no entity holding.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — gate `driftX`/`driftDir` advance in `_moveEnemies()` on no entity holding.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — extend the shared `EnemyEntity` seam with the optional `requiresFormationHold` method.
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — seam unit tests (state → hold true/false across the cycle).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — freeze/resume integration tests (single and multiple divers; non-Diver formation still drifts; respawn suppressed during a hold).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `_moveEnemies` freeze/resume test (ping-pong drift preserved).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document the formation hold and update the E2/behaviour tables.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — GDD §4.1 E2: note that the cluster holds while a Diver is away.

## Related work

- `AH-0MU0EIDQQ003S1JT` — *Diver should pause before returning* (completed): introduced `DiverState.PAUSING` with a configurable 500 ms pause. This item extends the attack window that now holds the formation.
- `AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB` — *Fix Diver.ts: lock x during dive and smooth return to current formation slot* (completed) and `AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD` — *Diver jumps on return from dive* (completed): established the smooth return onto the *current* slot, which AC3 preserves.
- `AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX` — *Diver should rotate to face the player and dive towards them* (completed): made the dive diagonal and player-targeted; preserved by AC4/Q3-A.
- `AH-0MUEI8HSU000QLEA` — *Diver docs stale: dive described as x-locked but implemented as diagonal* (open): related documentation discrepancy, explicitly **not** folded into this item.
- `AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW` — *GymDiver AC1 … wall-clock flaky under full-suite parallel load* (completed): determinism precedent for the new tests (tick-driven, no wall-clock).
- `AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4` — *Stale formation entities crash on GymEnemies scene restart* (completed): the `_localPhase`/no-`scene`-deref constraint that the seam must respect (no new `scene` dereference in the Diver).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (documented, Q2-B):** `PAUSING` counts as "away", so the freeze covers all non-`FORMATION` states. This keeps the cluster stationary for the entire attack rather than twitching during the 500 ms pause.
- **Risk — long freezes when divers are desynchronised.** All divers share the same hold timer, so they normally dive together and the cluster freezes for the attack window (~3.3 s of a ~6.3 s cycle). If divers become desynchronised (destruction and later respawn), the cluster could be held for extended periods. Mitigation: the hold is released as soon as no diver is detached; monitor during playtest and tune the hold timing if it reads poorly.
- **Risk — ping-pong drift state.** In `PlayScene` the freeze must not corrupt `driftDir`; the resume test must assert direction continuity.
- **Risk — destroyed divers.** A Diver destroyed mid-dive/return must stop holding the formation (its `alive` flag is false / it is removed). Add a test so a dead Diver cannot freeze the cluster forever.
- **Assumption:** non-Diver formations and asteroid roaming are unaffected; the seam is optional and only the Diver implements it.
- **Scope-creep risk:** gap-closing/restructuring (`Q2-C`) and wrap-only relocation (`Q2-D`) were offered and not selected; any such ideas should be recorded as linked work items rather than added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

The seed description was ambiguous, so the Diver behaviour was confirmed by the producer before the brief was finalised.

- **Q1 — Does "Divers should not return" mean they must not return at all, or that they must not return to the stale start point?** — **Answer (producer): "1. a" → they still return, but to their slot in the *current* formation, never to the dive-start point.** Source: interactive reply. Consequence: AC3; no state-machine removal of the return.

# Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

# Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

# Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

# Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

# Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audit/` or equivalent audit runner module — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`, `_build_issue_json`, in-main-slot verdict handling
- `scripts/audit_runner*` or equivalent — runner invocation, non-interactive path
- Audit output/summary formatter — diagnostic message generation

# Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic (completed): the parent epic that discovered this issue during audit.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** — Audit parent-first flow (internal assertion): the flow that triggers the re-audit on stale children.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — Audit in-main-slot mode (internal assertion): the mode that creates `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fingerprint scoping is incomplete.** If child-relevant files/commits are not correctly identified, stale audits may still be invalidated or, conversely, genuinely stale audits may be reused. Mitigation: carefully identify the key files that each child audit covers; add a test case that simulates unrelated HEAD movement vs. child-relevant HEAD movement.
- **Risk — inheriting stale child verdicts masks real regressions.** If a child's code changed but the fingerprint didn't catch it, inheriting an old verdict is incorrect. Mitigation: the fingerprint scoping should cover all files relevant to the child audit.
- **Assumption:** all three suggested directions are desired (fingerprint scoping, partial-verdict handling, diagnostic clarity).
- **Assumption:** the audit runner is a Node.js/TypeScript or Python tool within the project; the fix applies to the runner's Python/TS source.

# Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation

## Problem statement

The runtime auto-sequencer (`src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`, AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is a standalone pure-core library — nothing in the playable game calls it. Enemy composition is still hard-coded in `src/waves/Formations.ts` (`LEVELS`) and driven through `WaveManager` by `PlayScene`, so every run uses the same fixed waves. This item wires the sequencer into a playable run so wave composition is generated at runtime from a target difficulty curve, behind an opt-in config toggle, with the static campaign preserved as the default and the fallback.

## Users

- As a **player**, when the feature is enabled, enemy waves should follow a difficulty curve so each run ramps up smoothly instead of using identical fixed enemy counts. (Default-off means shipped behaviour is unchanged until enabled.)
- As a **designer**, I want to define the campaign's levels, names, wave counts and per-wave difficulty targets in a CSV config, so I can tune the difficulty ramp and campaign shape without editing `Formations.ts`.

## Decisions confirmed at intake

1. **Opt-in toggle, default off.** Static `LEVELS` remains the shipped default; generated waves only drive the run when the toggle is enabled in config. A follow-on work item covers *mixing* generated and scripted levels within one campaign: **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** (sibling, `discovered-from`).
2. **Per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.** One `sequencer()` call per level; the curve length sets the wave count.
3. **Fully data-driven campaign skeleton.** The curve config also defines the level count and level names (not just targets). The boss is still triggered after the final configured level (existing `WaveManager` behaviour).
4. **CSV-backed config.** A new `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is loaded through the existing `configStore`/CSV pipeline (editable in dev via `/api/csv/...`, bundled read-only in production).
5. **Defaults seeded from current calibration.** The baked-in default targets are derived from the current `LEVELS` measured scores (`levelDifficulty`/`enemyDifficulty`) spread non-decreasingly across each level's waves.

## Existing state

- `WaveManager` already accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` via its constructor and `setLevels()`, defaulting to static `LEVELS`; it owns plan/spawn/progression and the boss trigger.
- `sequencer(curve, candidates, options)` returns one `ShootableWave` per curve entry, each with one adjusted group and a `shootEnabled` flag; `options.defaultShootEnabled` applies to the whole call, which is why generation is done **per level** (so Levels 1–3 and 4–5 can differ).
- `AdjustedGroup` extends `WaveGroup`, so `ShootableWave.groups` maps structurally to `WaveDefinition.groups`.
- Config tunables live in two pipelines: CSV-backed `configStore`/`csv.ts`/Vite plugin (enemies, ship) and the localStorage-backed `rules.ts` (`GameRules`).
- GDD §2.4 — Levels 1–3 do not fire; §2.5 — Levels 4–5 do. §3.2 fixes level themes.

## Desired change

At run start, `PlayScene` reads the config. When the (opt-in) toggle is disabled it uses static `LEVELS` exactly as today. When enabled it builds a `LevelDefinition[]` from the difficulty-curve config by calling `sequencer()` once per configured level with `defaultShootEnabled = levelNumber >= 4`, converts each `ShootableWave` to a `WaveDefinition`, injects the result into `WaveManager`, and drives the run from it. Any empty/degenerate config falls back to static `LEVELS`.

## Constraints

- **Pure core stays pure.** `difficultySequencer.ts` is not modified (read-only call site).
- **Determinism.** Generation must be a pure function of config + candidate pool; no RNG.
- **No behavioural change when the toggle is off.** Existing `WaveManager`/`PlayScene`/campaign tests must pass unchanged.
- **CSV is the source of truth in dev**; production reads the bundled copy; malformed rows must not crash.
- Follow the existing config/CSV patterns (codec, plugin, store) rather than inventing a new persistence path.
- UK English in prose; Markdown in the work item.

## Assumptions

- The global opt-in toggle is a scalar tunable and will live in the existing `GameRules` settings store (`sequencedWavesEnabled`, default `false`); the per-level curve values/targets live in the CSV. Per-level source mixing is deferred to AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD.
- The campaign fire rule is derived from the (1-based) level number: `level <= 3` ⇒ `shootEnabled=false`, `level >= 4` ⇒ `true`. With a data-driven skeleton this applies to any configured levels beyond 5 as firing levels; per-level `shootEnabled` overrides are out of scope.
- "Configurable curve" is satisfied by the CSV-backed config plus the baked-in default; runtime UI editing is AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL.

## Acceptance criteria

- **WaveManager accepts injected definitions** — `WaveManager` is driven by generated `LevelDefinition`/`WaveDefinition` data; with no override supplied it uses static `LEVELS` exactly, and existing `WaveManager` tests pass unchanged.
- **Opt-in toggle** — with the toggle disabled (the default) the run uses static `LEVELS` and behaves as today; with it enabled the run uses generated definitions (test asserts both paths).
- **Runtime generation runs** — at run start, with the toggle enabled, the game builds per-level curves from the curve config and calls `sequencer()` once per level, obtaining a `SequencerResult` per level.
- **CSV-backed, data-driven config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` defines level number, level name and per-wave targets (curve length ⇒ wave count); it is loaded through the existing CSV/configStore pipeline and is editable in dev / read-only in production. Malformed or missing rows fall back to the baked-in default curve without crashing.
- **Generated waves drive the run** — the groups produced by the sequencer are what `PlayScene` spawns (verified via the spawn plan / `WaveManager.planSpawns()` or a test harness), not the static `LEVELS`.
- **Curve is configurable** — changing the configured/default curve changes the produced wave composition; two distinct curves yield different plans (test asserts this).
- **Campaign fire rule** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false`; levels 4+ have `shootEnabled=true` (test asserts both).
- **Determinism** — generating the campaign twice with the same config and candidate pool yields identical level/wave definitions.
- **Fallback is safe** — an empty/degenerate curve config, an empty curve, or an empty candidate pool falls back to static `LEVELS` and the game does not crash (test covers the fallback).
- **Testing/validation** — new unit/integration tests cover the codec, campaign builder, conversion, fire rule, determinism and fallback, and they are meaningful and passing.
- **Documentation** — all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **No regressions** — the full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — existing sequencer; read-only call site (`sequencer`, `defaultCandidatePool`, `ShootableWave`, `AdjustedGroup`).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — add a difficulty-curve codec (parse/serialize + validation, mirroring `EnemyConfig`).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add the difficulty-curve row/config types (leaf module, no imports).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — load `difficulty-curves.csv` through the existing dev/bundled pipeline and expose an accessor.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — add the opt-in `sequencedWavesEnabled` tunable (default `false`) to `GameRules`.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — **new** CSV defining levels, names, wave targets (data-driven skeleton).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — **new**: build the curve config/pool and convert `SequencerResult` per level into `LevelDefinition[]` (plus fallback).
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — confirm/verify injected-definition support (minimal or no change).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static `LEVELS`: default/fallback and level metadata source for seeding defaults.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — build + inject the generated campaign at run start when the toggle is enabled.
- Vite CSV plugin / dev write endpoint — extend to serve the new CSV if the existing generic path does not already cover it.
- Test files: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` (**new**), `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **CSV pipeline scope** — extending the codec/plugin/store is the largest cost; mitigated by mirroring the existing `EnemyConfig` codec/plugin exactly and reusing the generic write endpoint where possible.
- **Default-curve calibration drift** — seeding from measured `LEVELS` scores could diverge from the static campaign if either changes; mitigated by a test asserting the default generated campaign is non-decreasing and stays in 0–100.
- **Fallback correctness** — a partial/degenerate CSV must never produce an unplayable campaign; mitigated by an explicit fallback test and a single guard at the PlayScene boundary.
- **Scope creep** — runtime curve editing (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL) and mixed generated/scripted campaigns (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD) are explicitly out of scope; extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items rather than absorbed here.
- **Assumption (toggle location)** — the opt-in toggle lives in the `GameRules`/settings store rather than the CSV; revisit only if the producer prefers an all-CSV toggle.

## Out of scope

- Player-state adaptation (adjusting the curve from player performance).
- Runtime curve editing UI (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL).
- Replacing boss / asteroid spawning logic.
- Per-level generated-vs-scripted mixing (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD).

## Related work

- **Implement runtime auto-sequencer for dynamic difficulty adjustment (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X)** — delivered the sequencer this item wires in (`discovered-from`).
- **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** — follow-on enabled by the opt-in toggle (sibling).
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** — sibling designer tool; previews curves but does not affect the game.
- **Design a mechanism for calculating how hard an enemy is to survive (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K)** — delivered the `enemyDifficulty`/`levelDifficulty` scorer and campaign calibration that seed the default curve.
- **Config store / CSV pipeline (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA)** — the persistence pattern the new curve CSV follows.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.4/§2.5 fire rules, §3.2 level themes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — enemy archetypes/formations.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (Round 1): Does the generated sequence replace `LEVELS` outright, or sit behind a toggle?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) opt-in, default off** — shipped behaviour stays unchanged until a designer enables it. Additionally the operator asked for a follow-on work item allowing a campaign to **mix generated and scripted levels**.
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Follow-up: created **Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)**.

- **Q (Round 1): Per-level curves or one whole-run curve?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) per-level curves with configurable per-level wave counts.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: the sequencer takes a single `defaultShootEnabled` for a whole call and returns one group per curve entry — a whole-run curve cannot vary the fire rule by level. Read `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`.

- **Q (Round 1): Where does the curve (and its override) live?**
  - Answer (operator): **(b) extend the CSV `configStore` with a new difficulty-curve file.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: `configStore`/`csv.ts` are CSV-backed and read-only in production; `rules.ts` is the localStorage tunables store. Read `src/core/configStore.ts`, `src/core/csv.ts`.

- **Q (Round 2): When generated mode is enabled, does the campaign skeleton stay fixed?**
  - Answer (operator): **(a) config also defines level count and names — fully data-driven campaign.**
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Note: boss still triggers after the final configured level via existing `WaveManager` behaviour.

- **Q (Round 2): How editable is the new difficulty-curve CSV?**
  - Answer (operator): **as recommended** — route it through the existing CSV pipeline (editable in dev, bundled read-only in production).
  - Source: interactive reply.

- **Q (Round 2): Where do the default target values come from?**
  - Answer (operator): **as recommended** — seed per-level defaults from the current `LEVELS` measured scores, spread non-decreasingly across waves.
  - Source: interactive reply.
  - Research: `levelDifficulty(LEVELS[i].waves).score` in `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`; campaign calibration regression in `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`.

# Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign

## Problem statement

**Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63)** makes the campaign all-or-nothing: with `sequencedWavesEnabled` off every level uses the hand-authored static `LEVELS`, and with it on *every* level is generated from the difficulty-curve config. A designer cannot hand-tune the levels that matter (onboarding, boss lead-in, a specific set-piece) while letting the sequencer ramp the rest. This item lets a single campaign **mix** generated and scripted levels, selected per level.

## Users

- As a **designer**, I want to mark individual levels as generated or scripted, so I can hand-tune onboarding and set-piece levels while the sequencer handles the rest.
- As a **player**, I want the campaign to keep its hand-authored early levels but ramp difficulty in later levels, so each run is both learnable and challenging.
- As a **maintainer**, I want a single, data-driven campaign definition whose generated and scripted sources are explicit and testable, so the two paths cannot silently diverge.

## Decisions confirmed at intake

1. **Selector is an explicit `source` column in `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`** (`generated` | `scripted`). `source` defaults to `generated` when absent, so the existing 4-column CSV and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` keep working unchanged. For `scripted` rows `targetDifficulty` is optional/ignored (the level's waves come from `LEVELS`, not the curve). A level number must declare one consistent source; rows that disagree are malformed.
2. **Campaign skeleton starts from static `LEVELS`.** The merged campaign contains all static levels 1–5 (used verbatim when a level is `scripted` or unlisted), overrides a level when configured as `generated`, and appends configured generated levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT` in ascending order. Result is sorted ascending by `level`.
3. **Fallback is per-level.** A `generated` level with an empty/malformed curve (or a `sequencer` throw) falls back to that level's static `LEVELS` definition when one exists; a generated level with no static counterpart (number beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`) is skipped. Whole-campaign fallback to static `LEVELS` only when the candidate pool is empty or the resulting campaign would be empty. No path may yield an unplayable campaign or crash.

## Existing state

- **Campaign builder** — `buildSequencedLevels(rows?, candidates?)` in `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` groups `DifficultyCurveRow[]` by level, calls the read-only `sequencer()` once per generated level with `defaultShootEnabled = level >= FIRST_FIRING_LEVEL (4)`, converts `ShootableWave.groups` to `WaveGroup`s and returns `LevelDefinition[]`. On empty/degenerate input or a sequencer throw it returns static `LEVELS` (whole-campaign fallback). It has **no notion of a per-level source**.
- **Config** — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` is one row per `(level, wave)` with columns `level,levelName,wave,targetDifficulty`; loaded by `loadDifficultyCurves()` (`src/core/configStore.ts`) through the CSV pipeline (dev `/api/csv/...`, bundled `?raw` in production) with `defaultDifficultyCurves()` computed from the static `LEVELS` calibration as the fallback. Types live in `src/core/configTypes.ts` (`DifficultyCurveRow`); codec/validator in `src/core/csv.ts` (`parseDifficultyCurves` / `serializeDifficultyCurves` / `validateDifficultyCurveRow`). Malformed files fall back wholesale to the computed default curve.
- **Static campaign** — `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`: five `LevelDefinition`s (names, waves, `shootEnabled`). Levels 1–3 do not fire; 4–5 do (GDD §2.4/§2.5).
- **Wiring** — `PlayScene` exposes `resolveCampaignLevels(rules, build)`: toggle off ⇒ static `LEVELS`; toggle on ⇒ `buildSequencedLevels()`, falling back to `LEVELS` on empty/throw. `GameRules.sequencedWavesEnabled` (default `false`) lives in `src/core/rules.ts`. `WaveManager` accepts injected `LevelDefinition[]` and progresses by **array index** — `WaveManager.level` is `index + 1`, so `LevelDefinition.level` is display metadata and the merged array must be ordered ascending.

## Desired change

Extend the campaign builder so each level's source is selectable, and merge the two sources into one ordered `LevelDefinition[]`:

- A level marked **`generated`** is produced by `sequencer()` from that level's curve rows (as today, `shootEnabled` from the level's fire rule).
- A level marked **`scripted`** is taken **byte-for-byte from static `LEVELS`** (its own waves and `shootEnabled`) and is never passed to the sequencer.
- All static levels remain present unless overridden; generated levels beyond the static five are appended. See the confirmed decisions above.

When `sequencedWavesEnabled` is **off**, behaviour is unchanged: static `LEVELS` exactly. Mixed mode is only reachable with the toggle on.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Fire rule per source** — generated levels 1–3 have `shootEnabled=false` and 4+ `true`; scripted levels keep `LEVELS`' own flags (test asserts both).
- **Per-level fallback is safe** — a generated level with an empty/malformed curve falls back to its static `LEVELS` definition while the rest of the mixed campaign is preserved; a generated level with no static counterpart is skipped; an empty candidate pool or an empty resulting campaign falls back to static `LEVELS`; none of these crash (test covers each case).

# Phase Shift — auto-apply when the player is in danger

## Problem statement

Phase Shift (P6) currently grants a fixed 3 s of intangibility when collected (or permanently when chosen from the hold-full reward), which does not fit the game's moment-to-moment play: the player has to anticipate danger and activate at the right time, and the reward is frequently wasted. We want Phase Shift to become an **automatic, reactive defensive tool** that fires the instant the player is in real danger, lasts long enough to escape (1.5 s), and is unmistakably communicated through audio-visual "juice". A permanently-bought Phase Shift grants unlimited uses; a normally-collected one grants a finite number of uses.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, when I am about to be overwhelmed by enemies or bullets, I want my Phase Shift to trigger automatically so I can escape without having to track a timer or press a key, and I want the screen to clearly tell me I am intangible."
- **Player (permanent purchase):** "As a player who chose Phase Shift from the hold-full reward, I want unlimited automatic phase shifts for the rest of the run so the reward feels genuinely powerful."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want the danger-detection and auto-trigger logic to live in the shared power-up layer so the shipped game and every combat gym behave identically (no divergent copies)."

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `EffectsRegistry` owns P6 as a timed effect (`P6_PHASE_DURATION = 3`); `applyPhaseShift()` activates/refreshes it (used by P7 teleport), `applyCollect('P6', permanent?)` starts it, `isPhased` / `isHitImmune` read it. `permanent` (hold-full choice) never expires.
- Collision gating already respects phase: `CombatScene.isPlayerPhased()` → `getEffectsRegistry().isPhased`; `_handleCollisions()` skips the enemy-bullet-vs-player and player-vs-enemy passes while phased. `PlayScene._handleAsteroidCollisions()` has an equivalent early return.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` draws the shared P6 ghost (ship alpha `0.45`, blink-aware) via `applyPhaseGhost()`, used by `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `SHIP_SIZE = 20`, `PLAYER_BULLET_RADIUS = 3`, player hull = `SHIP_SIZE / 2`.
- Mineral collection lives in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` and `PlayScene` (`_collectMineral` / `onPlayerCollected`); nothing currently blocks collection while phased.
- Juice precedent: `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` (camera shake + flash + particles, per-layer toggles) and `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`; procedural WebAudio cues live in `src/audio/effects.ts` (all safe no-ops without an AudioContext, so headless tests never break).
- No danger-detection / proximity-threat logic exists today.

## Desired change

1. **Danger detection** — each frame, count hostile threats whose centre lies within `DANGER_RADIUS = 2 × SHIP_SIZE` (40 px) of the ship: enemy bodies (including asteroids, boss and minions) plus live enemy bullets. When the combined count reaches `DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD = 3`, the player is "in danger".
2. **Auto-trigger (P6 charge)** — when in danger and a Phase Shift charge is available (or the run holds the permanent Phase Shift), automatically activate Phase Shift for `PHASE_DURATION = 1.5 s`. A normally-collected P6 grants a stored auto-activation charge; the permanent (hold-full) P6 grants unlimited activations.
3. **Pass-through / collection gate** — while phased, bullets and enemies pass straight through the player (already implemented) and the player **cannot collect minerals** (new gate).
4. **Juice** — screen-wide, unmistakable phase feedback: all on-screen enemies, bullets and minerals are visually distorted/faded/shaken (e.g. chromatic-aberration style split-tint or desaturation + shake), the ship keeps its ghost alpha, and a distinct sci-fi Phase Shift sound plays on every activation.
5. **P7 teleport unchanged in mechanic** — teleport still activates Phase Shift on arrival; only the duration becomes 1.5 s (assumption; see Open Questions).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Danger detection is measurable and correct.** A pure, unit-testable helper counts hostile entities + hostile bullets within `2 × SHIP_SIZE` of the ship and reports "in danger" when the combined count is ≥ 3. Boundary cases are covered: exactly 3 threats triggers; 2 threats do not; threats just inside the radius count and just outside do not; asteroids, boss/minions and all enemy bullet types count; player bullets and minerals do not.
- [ ] **AC2 — Auto-trigger semantics.** When in danger and a P6 activation is available, Phase Shift activates automatically for exactly 1.5 s without any player input, and the 1.5 s countdown replaces the old 3 s duration everywhere (drop, hold-full, P7 arrival). The re-arm rule after expiry is implemented per the producer answer to Q2 (danger must clear below threshold before re-arming, plus a ~0.5 s re-arm cooldown) and unit-tested for both the charge and permanent cases.
- [ ] **AC3 — Charges and permanence.** A normally-collected P6 grants a finite number of auto-activations (one per pickup, per the producer answer to Q3) that is decremented on trigger and visible in the HUD; a hold-full permanent P6 grants unlimited activations. Tests cover: charge consumed on trigger, no trigger with zero charges, permanent triggers repeatedly.
- [ ] **AC4 — Pass-through and mineral gate.** While phased, enemy bodies and bullets do not hit the player (existing behaviour retained, regression-tested) and mineral collection is blocked; mineral collection resumes immediately after expiry. Power-up / weapon drop collection behaviour is per Open Question Q7.
- [ ] **AC5 — Juice and audio.** On every Phase Shift activation, all on-screen enemies, bullets and minerals receive the shared phase visual treatment (fade/shake and/or global distortion) for the duration of the effect and it is cleanly cleared on expiry; the ship ghost remains. A dedicated sci-fi Phase Shift WebAudio cue plays on activation and degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext. The visual layers are toggleable (mirroring `playerDeathJuice`) and unit-tested for state transitions; audio presence is asserted via the existing audio-test seams.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation.** New automated unit/integration tests cover danger detection, auto-trigger timing, charge/permanent semantics, the mineral gate and visual/audio wiring, and they fail against the pre-change implementation (TDD where practical). Manual `npm run dev` check confirms the visual/audio feedback reads clearly in-game.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 P6/P7 entries) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` hit-gating notes. (`CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the release pipeline and is excluded.)
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Engine-agnostic logic stays in `src/powerups` (no Phaser imports), mirroring the existing registry/test split; rendering and audio stay in scenes / `src/vfx` / `src/audio`.
- The single shared combat path must be preserved: `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymFormationScene` must all inherit the same auto-trigger behaviour (no per-scene copies) — enforced by the existing cross-scene equivalence tests.
- Audio must remain a safe no-op without an AudioContext (headless tests must not break).
- Exclude CI/CD pipeline tests and `CHANGELOG.md` from the ACs.
- Do not regress P7 teleport safety or the existing P3/P6 hit-gating.

## Desired change / behaviour summary

The player no longer manages Phase Shift actively. The ship "phases out" on its own the moment three or more threats close within two ship-widths, escapes through them for 1.5 s, and the whole screen visibly and audibly "shifts" to sell the effect. Collecting P6 stock-piles finite auto-uses; the hold-full reward makes them unlimited.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — Add `DANGER_RADIUS` (2 × `SHIP_SIZE`), `DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD` (3), `PHASE_DURATION` (1.5); retire/supersede `P6_PHASE_DURATION = 3`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Replace/extend P6 timed-effect model with charge + permanent auto-activation; expose danger trigger state, charge count per activation, and a hook the scene calls with "in danger".
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` (new) — Pure proximity/danger helper (threat count within radius), unit-tested.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — Feed live enemy/bullet positions into the danger check each frame; own the auto-trigger call and the mineral-collection gate.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Wire danger detection, mineral gate, and the new juice/sound on activation.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — Ensure the gym shares the same auto-trigger and visual treatment.
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` (new) — Screen-wide phase visual treatment (fade/shake/distortion), layer toggles for tests.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playPhaseShiftSound()` (sci-fi cue, safe no-op without AudioContext).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Surface finite P6 charges (if Q3 chooses charges).
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/vfx/*.test.ts` — New/updated coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `README.md` — Documentation updates.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** the juice work (chromatic aberration / screen distortion) can balloon. Keep it to one shared, toggleable module; record anything beyond the agreed aesthetic as a linked follow-up rather than expanding scope.
- **Balance risk:** if Phase Shift re-arms while still surrounded, a permanent P6 can make the player permanently invincible. The re-arm rule (Q2) is the key mitigation and must be decided before implementation.
- **Confirmed (Q5):** all hostile bullets and enemy bodies (asteroids, boss, minions, all enemy archetypes) count as threats; player bullets and minerals do not.
- **Assumption:** `2 × ship size` means a 40 px centre-to-centre radius (ship hull `SHIP_SIZE / 2`).
- **Assumption:** danger detection is evaluated once per frame in the shared combat core, so all combat scenes share it.
- **Confirmed (Q7):** only mineral collection is blocked while phased; power-up/weapon drops remain collectable.
- **Confirmed (Q6):** P7 teleport still grants a direct 1.5 s Phase Shift on arrival (an explicit escape, not danger-triggered, and it does not consume a danger charge).

## Related work

- `AH-0MTE8EBAH007GUO0` — Effects module: shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift, teleport (completed).
- `AH-0MTE8EBVD0010T0Z` — Unit tests: P6 Phase Shift — pass-through, expiry, refresh (completed; superseded semantics, keep history).
- `AH-0MU8QVC9Y008R8I5` — PlayScene: add P6 phase-shift ghost visual (completed).
- `AH-0MT7UY5UR002LD5U` — Redesign P7 Dash: make collectable teleport power-up (completed; P7 grants P6 on arrival).
- `AH-0MUDY2GH3003NYY3` / `AH-0MUDY2W27009VC2M` — Player-death juice parameter model + cross-path regression (completed; juice pattern to mirror).
- `AH-0MUHM66ES0027QQV` — Shared P3/P6 hit-gating in the formation gyms (completed).
- `AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4` — Hold-full rewards functional in every gym (completed).
- GDD §4.4 (`docs/Game Design Document.md`), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.2.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

All clarifying questions were answered by the producer during intake (interactive reply, session `herdr-1790480233-2106778-27856`). The accepted answers are recorded below and supersede the earlier `OPEN QUESTION` markers.

- **Q1 — Danger-count semantics.** Does "3 or more enemies or bullets within 2× the ship's size" mean the *combined* count of enemy bodies + hostile bullets within the radius ≥ 3, or separate thresholds? — Answer (producer): **combined**. Accepted: the combined count of all hostile threats (enemy bodies incl. asteroids/boss/minions plus enemy bullets) whose centre is within 40 px (2 × `SHIP_SIZE`) of the ship, threshold ≥ 3. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Re-arm after the 1.5 s expires.** If the player is still in danger when the 1.5 s ends, may Phase Shift immediately re-trigger? — Answer (producer): **as recommended**. Accepted: the danger condition must clear below the threshold before the effect can re-arm, plus a short ~0.5 s re-arm cooldown (a permanent P6 is powerful but not perpetual invincibility). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Non-permanent P6 pickup model.** What does a normally-collected P6 grant now that pickup no longer activates a 3 s effect? — Answer (producer): **as recommended**. Accepted: one stored auto-activation charge per pickup (consumed on trigger, shown in the HUD); the hold-full permanent reward grants unlimited charges. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 — Juice aesthetic.** Chromatic split-tint on enemies/bullets/minerals vs fade + shake? — Answer (producer): **as recommended**. Accepted: one shared, toggleable screen-wide module — subtle desaturation/dim + a chromatic split-tint on enemies/bullets/minerals, a light camera shake on activation, and a rising sci-fi whoosh/chirp. VFX values remain tunable in implementation. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5 — Threat scope.** Do asteroids, the Central AI boss and boss minions count as dangers, and do player bullets/minerals? — Answer (producer): **as recommended**. Accepted: all hostile bodies (asteroids, boss, minions, every enemy archetype) and all enemy bullets count; player bullets and minerals do not. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q6 — P7 teleport interaction.** Does P7 teleport still directly activate Phase Shift on arrival, now at 1.5 s? — Answer (producer): **as recommended**. Accepted: yes — teleport is an explicit escape, activates a 1.5 s Phase Shift directly and does not consume a danger-triggered charge. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q7 — Collection gate scope during phase.** Should power-up/weapon drops also be blocked while phased? — Answer (producer): **as recommended**. Accepted: only mineral collection is blocked while phased; power-up/weapon drops remain collectable. Source: interactive reply.

# Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration

## Goal

As a **designer**, I want to mark each configured wave with a **generation mode**, so one campaign can mix hand-authored set-pieces with curve-driven and runtime-regenerated waves.

Three modes (the default is (a)):

- **(a) `curve` — curve-generated, fixed at runtime.** The sequencer builds the wave from its `targetDifficulty` once; the composition is then fixed for the whole run. It only changes when the designer explicitly asks for a level/wave regeneration (the `Regenerate` action).
- **(b) `fixed` — hand-authored, never regenerated.** The wave composition is authored and used verbatim at design and runtime. It is never passed through the sequencer. Its difficulty is *derived* from its settings (shown read-only in the editor — see sibling item 2).
- **(c) `dynamic` — regenerated at runtime.** The wave is rebuilt from its curve by the sequencer at runtime, seeded from the run's RNG, so successive runs differ while remaining reproducible for a given seed.

## Context / existing state

- `DifficultyCurveRow` — `src/core/configTypes.ts:88` — currently `level`, `levelName`, `wave`, `targetDifficulty`.
- Codec/validation — `src/core/csv.ts:405` (`DIFFICULTY_CURVE_COLUMN_ORDER`, `parseDifficultyCurves`, `serializeDifficultyCurves`, `validateDifficultyCurveRow`) and the Vite dev writer `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`.
- Seeded config — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`.
- Builder — `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` (`buildSequencedLevels`), currently pure/deterministic and always curve-generated.
- Runtime wiring — `resolveCampaignLevels`/`PlayScene.create` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:202,405`) and `WaveManager.setLevels` (`src/waves/WaveManager.ts:103`).
- Editor preview — `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.

## Relationships

- **Supersedes / generalises Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** to per-wave granularity and adds the `dynamic` mode. Reconcile at intake: preferred outcome is that this item absorbs that scope and AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD is closed as superseded or reduced to any residual per-level behaviour.
- Enables the sibling UI item (generation-mode control in the curve generator) and the default-on item.

## Desired behaviour

- Add a `generation` column (`curve` | `fixed` | `dynamic`) to `DifficultyCurveRow`, the codec (`DIFFICULTY_CURVE_COLUMN_ORDER`, parse/serialize/validate), the Vite plugin whitelist and the seed CSV. An **absent** value means `curve`, so existing 4-column files and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` keep working unchanged.
- The builder honours the mode per wave:
  - `curve`: unchanged — one sequencer call per level, composition fixed for the run.
  - `fixed`: use the hand-authored composition verbatim; **never** call the sequencer for that wave.
  - `dynamic`: call the sequencer at wave-build time using an injectable run seed/RNG so the wave differs between runs but is reproducible for a given seed.
- Determinism contract: `curve` and `fixed` waves are independent of the seed; `dynamic` waves are a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed).
- Fallback: missing/unknown mode ⇒ `curve`; a malformed mode is treated like any other malformed row (dropped, existing file-level default-curve fallback preserved). A `fixed` wave whose composition cannot be resolved must fall back safely, never crash the run.
- **Open decision (resolve at intake):** where a `fixed` wave's composition is stored. Preferred: reuse the hand-authored static `LEVELS` wave for the same level/wave number. Alternative: persist an explicit serialized composition (groups) in the campaign config. Document whichever is chosen, including behaviour for levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The generation-mode column round-trips: `parseDifficultyCurves(serializeDifficultyCurves(rows))` preserves each wave's mode.
- Absent mode defaults to `curve`; existing 4-column CSV rows and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` output are unchanged.
- `fixed` waves are never passed to the sequencer (assertable via a spy/injected sequencer) and match their authored composition exactly.
- `dynamic` waves differ between at least two distinct seeds, and are identical for the same seed (test asserts both).
- `curve` and `fixed` waves are identical regardless of seed.
- Malformed/unknown mode rows and unresolvable `fixed` waves degrade safely (no crash; campaign remains playable).
- The Vite dev writer accepts valid `generation` values and rejects an invalid value with HTTP 400.
- Documentation (README, GDD, design doc and module comments) describes the three modes, the default and the seed/RNG contract for `dynamic`.
- New unit/integration tests cover the codec, mode dispatch, seed determinism and `fixed` sourcing; the full suite passes.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `generation` to `DifficultyCurveRow`.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — extend the difficulty-curve codec/validator.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — whitelist/validate the new column.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — add the column to the seed config.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — mode dispatch, seed threading and `fixed` sourcing.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `defaultDifficultyCurves()` mode defaults.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — thread the run seed into the builder for `dynamic` waves.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — verify injection seam; minimal change expected.
- Tests: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`.

## Goal

As a **designer**, working in the Dev Utilities curve generator (gym scene), I want a per-wave **generation-mode** control (`curve` | `fixed` | `dynamic`, default `curve`) so I can set each wave's behaviour from the editor. When I choose `fixed`, the difficulty slider must be **read-only** and show the difficulty **derived from that wave's current settings**.

## Context / existing state

- Curve editor/preview scene — `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), surfaced under **Dev Utilities** on the gym index.
- Each wave is a row with a 0–100 target slider (`data-curve-wave`), a value readout (`data-curve-wave-value`) and a Remove button; the panel has Add Wave and Regenerate, and an edit-to-clear stale state (`CURVE_PREVIEW_STALE_TEXT`).
- The generation-mode capability it exposes is delivered by the sibling item *Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration*. This item is the UI only; it must not reimplement the mode engine.

## Desired behaviour

- Each wave row gains a labelled mode control with exactly three options — `curve`, `fixed`, `dynamic` — defaulting to `curve`.
- Selecting `fixed`:
  - the target-difficulty slider becomes read-only/disabled;
  - the slider/readout shows the difficulty **computed from the wave's current (fixed) settings**, not an editable target;
  - the value is clearly presented as derived (e.g. a "fixed" affordance/label), not user-editable.
- Selecting `curve` or `dynamic` re-enables the editable target slider.
- Changing a wave's mode counts as an edit and marks the preview stale (existing edit-to-clear behaviour).
- Regenerate reflects the mode: `curve` and `dynamic` previews come from the sequencer; a `fixed` wave previews its authored composition and its derived difficulty.
- Mode choices must be persisted/reported through the same config path as the other wave fields (so the editor and the shipped CSV agree) — the exact persistence is shared with the sibling engine item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every curve row renders a generation-mode control offering `curve`, `fixed` and `dynamic`, defaulting to `curve`.
- Choosing `fixed` disables the target slider and displays the difficulty derived from the wave's current settings; the value cannot be edited through the slider.
- Choosing `curve` or `dynamic` re-enables the target slider and it is editable again.
- Changing a mode marks the preview stale and clears the wave list until Regenerate is pressed.
- Regenerating shows sequencer-derived previews for `curve`/`dynamic` waves and the authored composition plus derived difficulty for `fixed` waves.
- The control is keyboard accessible and labelled (no slider-dependent-only interaction).
- Unit/DOM tests (`GymCurveSequencer.test.ts`) cover default mode, the `fixed` read-only derived-difficulty behaviour, re-enabling, and the stale transition.
- The full suite passes.

## Out of scope

- The mode engine, CSV schema and runtime behaviour (sibling *Per-wave generation modes…* item).
- Saving/loading curves to the shipped CSV beyond what already exists; visual formation previews; drag-to-reorder.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — mode control, read-only derived slider, preview wiring.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.test.ts` — DOM/behaviour tests.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` / `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — consumed read-only for the derived difficulty.

# Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability

## Goal

As a **player**, the default (seeded) campaign should ramp difficulty smoothly and feel engaging, so enabling sequenced generation does not degrade the early game.

## Problem

The seeded default curve was derived mechanically from the static level measurements (see `defaultDifficultyCurves()` in `src/core/configStore.ts:114`). Measured evidence from the builder at HEAD `819429a` shows the generated campaign is degenerate in early levels:

| Level | Static | Generated (current defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Entry | `scout x6`, `scout x8` | `asteroid x1`, `asteroid x1` |
| 2 Descent | `scout x8`, `diver x8`, `swarm x10` | `asteroid x1`, `asteroid x1`, `scout x1` |
| 3 The Core | `tank6+scout4`, `diver6+scout4`, `tank6+swarm10` | `scout x1`, `scout x1`, `scout x1` |
| 4 Firestorm | `diver x6`, `tank x6`, `swarm x10` (fire) | `scout x18`, `swarm x15`, `diver x6` (fire) |
| 5 Predictable Death | `phaser x4`, `phaser x5` (fire) | `tank x1`, `phaser x4` (fire) |

Low early targets make the sequencer select the cheapest archetype (the non-firing asteroid) or a single-count group, so levels 1–3 are sparse and unengaging.

## Desired behaviour

- Retune the default difficulty curve (and, where appropriate, use the `fixed` generation mode from the sibling item for onboarding waves) so the default campaign:
  - removes degenerate early waves (no asteroid-only and no 1-count waves in levels 1–3);
  - keeps targets non-decreasing and within 0–100;
  - ramps smoothly across and within levels, preserving an intentional fire boundary (levels 1–3 do not fire; 4+ do);
  - yields wave compositions comparable in spirit to the hand-authored `LEVELS` (varied archetypes, sensible counts) while still being curve-driven where intended.
- Ensure the default campaign covers every configured level/wave with a playable composition and no empty/duplicate rows.
- Validate through the curve-generator preview and/or an automated spawn-plan assertion, not only by eye.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The default generated campaign contains **no** `asteroid`-only wave and **no** 1-count wave in levels 1–3 (test asserts on `buildSequencedLevels()` output / `WaveManager.planSpawns()`).
- Default target difficulties are non-decreasing within each level and across levels and stay within 0–100.
- Every configured wave yields a non-empty composition; aggregated difficulty increases from level 1 to the final level (no reversals).
- The fire boundary holds: levels 1–3 `shootEnabled=false`, levels 4+ `true`.
- The default curve is derived/stored consistently: `defaultDifficultyCurves()` and `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` agree, and codec/seed tests pass.
- A regression test pins the improved default campaign so a future change cannot silently reintroduce degenerate early waves.
- The full suite passes.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by *Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration* (so early onboarding waves can be `fixed` and the rest tuned against the new modes).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `defaultDifficultyCurves()` target values.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — seeded campaign targets/modes.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts`, `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — default/seed assertions.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` — default campaign regression assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts` — preview used for validation.
